findings.concave_points_vs_concavity: concave_points and concavity are distinct features with different geometric interpretations and clinical relevance. Concave points refer to the number of concave portions (specifically, the number of concave points per 100 pixels), while concavity refers to the degree of concavity (a measure of the curvature). In breast cancer diagnostics, concave points are often more directly related to tumor boundary irregularity and are strongly associated with malignancy. Concavity, on the other hand, is a more generalized curvature metric and may be less sensitive or more noise-prone. Both are used in the Wisconsin Breast Cancer Dataset, but concave points are typically more predictive and less redundant.
